findings.finding: Q2 2026 segment run-rate (wholesale $70.6M, DTC $31.4M, Outposts $5.0M = $107.0M) laid against Q3 2025 (wholesale $67.0M, DTC $27.8M, total $100.7M) implies Q3 revenue near $107M (+6%), about 1% above the $105.9M consensus and the company's '>=5%' guide floor; the company beat revenue by ~12% in Q1 and ~2.7% in Q2 and says the guide excludes further distribution wins and pricing, while also saying pricing benefits moderate from Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 revenue beat (+21% y/y, $109.2M vs ~$97.4M) with a guide raise: +23.85%. Q2 2026 beat ($107.0M vs ~$104.3M) with guide only affirmed: baseline records 0.0% (unverified; no source found for the Aug 4 move). Q3 2025 slight miss ($100.7M, -1.4% vs Zacks): -7.04%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus ($105.9M) sits exactly on the guide floor, so the street has not modelled the Q2 run-rate forward; if it had, Q3 estimates would sit at $107M+ rather than inside $104.9-106.5M. Thin coverage (3 analysts).
findings.independence: Q3 2025 comps from the Q3 2025 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1891101/000189110125000031/brcinc_exhibit991xq3fy2025.htm ; company Nielsen data on the Q2 call (packaged coffee +28.2% vs category +9.9%) https://www.webull.com/news/15344801058595840 . Shares the Q2 release with finding 2.

findings.finding: FY2026 guide arithmetic forces a choice at this print: H1 revenue is $216.2M, '>=8%' is ~$430M, so H2 needs only ~$214M vs H2 2025 $213.5M; the CFO said at the floor Q4 would be 'modestly below' prior year (lapping $5M of Q4 2025 liquidation sales). A Q3 near $107M with the floor held implies Q4 ~$106M, -6% y/y, so a revenue raise is the mechanical path, which is what the name paid +23.85% for in May; in August it held the guide after a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raise at Q1 2026 (to >=8% revenue / >=35% EBITDA): +23.85%. Guide affirmed at Q2 2026: ~0.0% per baseline (unverified).
findings.why_not_priced: FY consensus ~$432M (Yahoo) is barely above the floor, so a raise to e.g. >=9-10% is not in estimates; if priced, FY consensus would sit $5-10M higher. Partly offset: a +33% 20-day run-up with no company news may already anticipate it.
findings.independence: Yahoo FY consensus $432.21M https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BRCC/analysis/ . Same transcript underlies finding 3; Q2 release (finding 1) is the H1 figure source.
